about.heading: Curious about data, systems, and everything in between.
paragraphs: My name is Disu Ibukunoluwa. I'm a recent First Class Computer Science graduate from Covenant University and an emerging Data Engineer. I work with SQL, Python, and data visualisation tools, with experience in data modelling, dashboard design, and root-cause analysis that supports informed decision-making.

I became interested in data because it can help us understand what happened, see what is happening now, and spot patterns that might shape what happens next. That range of possibilities is what first sparked my curiosity.

But data doesn't become useful just because it exists. It has to be collected, organised, processed, stored, and made accessible. That's what draws me to Data Engineering: building the systems that connect information to the decisions people need to make.

When I'm not writing SQL or debugging code, I enjoy public speaking, debate, reading, and bringing people together to make ideas happen. I'm also fascinated by the universe and love falling down a rabbit hole whenever something catches my interest.

Those interests influence how I approach engineering. They've taught me to ask better questions, explain ideas clearly, and think about the people relying on a system. I'm always curious, always learning, and always looking for the next problem worth solving.
If you're into data, AI, or just want to talk about the universe over coffee, I'd love to connect!

projects_intro: A selection of practical projects showing how I approach data ingestion, transformation, reliability, and deployment. Explore the implementation details and engineering decisions behind each build.

projects.title: Bitcoin price ETL pipeline
projects.summary: An Apache Airflow ETL pipeline that collects Bitcoin prices in USD from the CoinMarketCap API, transforms them with Pandas, and loads them into PostgreSQL. If the database load fails, a timestamped CSV preserves the transformed data.
projects.challenge: Collect and standardise Bitcoin price data on a repeatable schedule for downstream analysis and reporting, while retaining the transformed output if PostgreSQL is unavailable during a load.
approach: Extract: Call CoinMarketCap's /v2/cryptocurrency/quotes/latest endpoint using an authenticated API request, with slug=bitcoin and convert=USD.
Transform: Use Pandas to normalise the JSON response into a DataFrame; remove unnecessary columns, rename fields, convert numeric values, and parse timestamps as datetimes.
Load: Write the transformed data to PostgreSQL. If the database load raises an exception, write a CSV file with a timestamped filename.
Orchestrate and deploy: Define extract_data_task, transform_data_task, and load_data_task in the crypto_dag Airflow DAG, and use GitHub Actions to deploy the workflow to an Ubuntu Airflow server.
projects.architecture: CoinMarketCap API (Bitcoin quotes in USD) → Airflow extraction → Pandas transformation → PostgreSQL, with a timestamped CSV fallback when the database load fails. The DAG is named crypto_dag, uses the monthly schedule 0 0 1 * * (first day of each month), and has a configured start date of 21 June 2024. GitHub Actions automates deployment to the Ubuntu server.

decisions.title: Separate ETL stages in Airflow
decisions.body: Extraction, transformation, and loading are separate tasks so each stage has a clear responsibility within the monthly DAG.

decisions.title: Keep a fallback when PostgreSQL fails
decisions.body: Save the transformed data to a timestamped CSV when the primary database write fails, avoiding the loss of that processed output.

decisions.title: Automate server deployment
decisions.body: Use a GitHub Actions workflow to deploy changes to the Ubuntu-hosted Airflow environment.

projects.quality: The load step handles PostgreSQL errors by preserving the transformed dataset in a timestamped CSV. This is a data-retention fallback rather than an automatic database replay mechanism.
projects.outcomes: Built a scheduled Bitcoin data ingestion and transformation workflow with PostgreSQL storage, failure fallback to CSV, and GitHub Actions deployment to an Ubuntu Airflow server. Its output can support cryptocurrency price analysis and reporting.
projects.lessons: Reliable ETL design includes more than a schedule: consistent data types, clear task boundaries, repeatable transformations, and a fallback for failures at the destination all matter.
